summary: This program stores a fisherman's haul of fish names in a list, including a repeated "Salmon", and sorts the list alphabetically so identical catches end up next to each other.

lines.text: A list happily holds the same value twice, which is exactly what we want here: the two salmon are both recorded rather than one overwriting the other.

The built-in sort function does the ordering for us, so we never have to write comparison logic of our own. It rearranges this list in place instead of handing back a new one, which is why nothing is assigned to a variable here.
Printing the list after sorting shows the fish in alphabetical order, and the duplicate salmon appear side by side so the fisherman can spot them at a glance.
